name: Skye Gui
title: Game & Interactive Design
intro: Skye Gui is a 2D Game Designer & Interactive Designer specializing in the creation of atmospheric narrative and puzzle experiences. Her work focuses on evocative environment storytelling and minimalist mechanics that invite deep immersion.
quote: My goal is to create distinctive interactive experiences where story, atmosphere, and gameplay feel like parts of the same world.
about: I am a 2D Game Designer and Interactive Designer currently studying the Master of Anime, Game and Interactive Design at RMIT University. With a background in spatial and graphic design, my practice focuses on atmospheric narrative, environmental storytelling, and puzzle-based interactive experiences.

I am interested in creating game worlds that encourage players to slow down, observe their surroundings, and gradually uncover stories through exploration and interaction. Rather than relying heavily on direct exposition, I use environments, objects, visual clues, characters, and puzzle mechanics to communicate narrative information.

My projects, including ISLAND, Wandering, and Raven, explore different ways of combining visual atmosphere, mystery, and interaction. I primarily work with GDevelop, Unity, Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign, and I continue to develop my practice across game design, visual development, and interactive storytelling.
My goal is to create distinctive interactive experiences where story, atmosphere, and gameplay feel like parts of the same world.

caseStudy.title: Turning Familiar Objects into Unsettling Clues
caseStudy.question: How can an ordinary object make a familiar space feel unsettling?
caseStudy.concept: ISLAND places the player in an unfamiliar setting where everyday objects carry fragments of a larger mystery. Its central design focus is observation: a furnished room, a photograph, or a handwritten message becomes meaningful when the player chooses to examine it. The intention is to make curiosity the starting point of the story.
caseStudy.interaction: The player inspects objects, collects and uses items, and moves between connected scenes. Close-up views shift attention from the room as a whole to individual clues. This creates a rhythm of looking, acting, and reconsidering what has already been seen, allowing exploration and puzzle solving to carry the narrative together.
caseStudy.visual: Domestic interiors sit alongside open water, a mist-covered pier, and a forest. The contrast gives each location a different emotional weight while maintaining the island's sense of isolation. The room's blue curtains and circular porthole provide clear visual anchors; the outdoor scenes use mist and distance to make the spaces beyond them harder to read. The draft-to-final comparisons show how composition, colour, and environmental detail contribute to that atmosphere.

references.heading: Inspiration — Rusty Lake
references.copy: [Rusty Lake](https://www.rustylake.com/), including its Cube Escape series, combines surreal mysteries with atmospheric point-and-click exploration. It is a key influence on ISLAND's use of familiar objects as unsettling clues. The relevant connection is the way observation, object interaction, and narrative discovery become parts of the same experience.

projects.name: Wandering

description: After falling into an unfamiliar world, a small wanderer finds three doors waiting ahead. Each opens onto a realm that is strange, beautiful, and quietly mysterious. Follow the symbols, explore unexpected landscapes, and solve puzzles along the way. With every threshold crossed, the world offers another glimpse of its secrets, inviting you to discover what lies beyond the next door.

caseStudy.title: Three Doors into the Unknown
caseStudy.question: How can opening a door feel like entering a different dream?
caseStudy.concept: Wandering begins with a simple invitation: three doors, each leading somewhere unknown. The small, white-cloaked figure gives the player a consistent point of connection as the surrounding world changes. The project explores the anticipation of crossing a threshold and the surprise of finding a space that follows its own visual logic.
caseStudy.interaction: Doors and symbols connect the experience's different scenes. Exploration and puzzles give the player reasons to look beyond a scene's first impression. The recurring figure and doorway motif help hold the journey together, allowing each new environment to introduce a different mood without losing the sense of one continuous adventure.
caseStudy.visual: The bright sky and ascending staircase contrast with violet water, moonlit buildings, and a quieter bedroom interior. Painterly textures give these distinct scenes a shared material quality. Against the coloured backgrounds, the character's simple silhouette stays easy to recognise. The draft-to-final comparisons can reveal how colour, architectural shapes, and character placement establish the identity of each space.

references.heading: Related work — Monument Valley
references.copy: [Monument Valley](https://ustwogames.co.uk/news/10-years-of-illusions-with-monument-valley/) brings a solitary figure into a world of impossible architecture and visual puzzles. It offers a useful reference for Wandering's relationship between a small character and an unfamiliar space. The comparison centres on dreamlike composition, visual clarity, and the anticipation of discovering a route forward.

projects.name: The Three-Day Funeral at Lawrence Manor
projects.imageAlt: The Three-Day Funeral at Lawrence Manor cover: the title and a birdcage-headed attendant in a misty forest
description: You arrive at Lawrence Manor to attend Mr. Lawrence's funeral, expecting a quiet farewell. A courteous welcome, a house half-hidden in mist, and a few seemingly ordinary details suggest that something is wrong. Look closer, follow the clues, and discover what waits behind the manor's doors. This house is far less peaceful than it first appears.

caseStudy.title: An Uneasy Welcome
caseStudy.question: How can a polite welcome make a player feel increasingly uneasy?
caseStudy.concept: The funeral gives the player a clear reason to approach Lawrence Manor, while the arrival scene introduces uncertainty about the place and its inhabitants. The opening focuses on small contradictions: formal manners, an isolated house, and a host whose appearance resists explanation. Curiosity grows from the gap between a welcoming gesture and an unsettling situation.
caseStudy.interaction: The supplied browser build follows the arrival sequence, the encounter with the birdcage-headed attendant, and the approach to the house. His written greetings lead into closer inspection of the entrance and mailbox. Moving between wider views and object close-ups lets an apparently ordinary detail become the next point of narrative attention.
caseStudy.visual: Layered grey mist softens the forest and obscures the house, while the attendant's silhouette remains clearly defined. The candle inside his birdcage and the warm entrance light provide small focal points within the restrained palette. The four draft/final pairs show the relationship between the surrounding landscape, the character encounter, the manor exterior, and the mailbox detail. Together, they move the visual focus from an uncertain destination toward a specific clue.

references.heading: Related work — What Remains of Edith Finch
references.copy: [What Remains of Edith Finch](https://www.giantsparrow.com/games/finch/) explores family history through stories centred on individual lives and deaths. It provides a useful narrative reference for making a house a place of remembrance and discovery. For Lawrence Manor, the relevant idea is that exploring a place can bring the lives associated with it into focus.

references.heading: Additional reference — The Last Door
references.copy: [The Last Door](https://store.steampowered.com/app/284390/The_Last_Door_-_Collector%27s_Edition) is a Gothic point-and-click mystery involving cryptic messages, abandoned places, and buried secrets. It offers a complementary reference for building suspense through investigation and withheld information. This comparison concerns narrative pacing and atmosphere, while Lawrence Manor retains its own hand-drawn visual identity.

projects.imageAlt: Raven cover: the title and a raven before four bright stained-glass windows
description: A raven arrives in a kingdom that once flourished and now lies fallen. Within its silent halls, the dead still whisper fragments of the past. Listen to their stories, explore what remains, and piece together the images and clues they leave behind. As the kingdom's history comes into focus, discover the truth beneath the remnants of its former splendour.

caseStudy.title: Piecing Together a Fallen Kingdom
caseStudy.question: How can a player uncover a kingdom's history through the people and images left behind?
caseStudy.concept: Raven follows an outsider entering a world shaped by a lost civilisation. The raven serves as a witness to the kingdom's remains, encountering figures whose stories bring the past into the present. The central intention is to turn the discovery of history into an active experience, with understanding emerging gradually through exploration.
caseStudy.interaction: Character conversations and image-based puzzles form the core of the experience. Encounters with the priest, queen, witch, and king provide narrative fragments, while assembling picture pieces makes reconstruction a physical action for the player. Bringing an image together echoes the larger task of piecing together the kingdom's history.
caseStudy.visual: Dark halls, repeated arches, and luminous stained-glass windows establish a world whose grandeur is still visible. Blue and violet tones surround sharp accents of cyan and gold, creating a contrast between the raven's dark silhouette and the architecture. The scene comparisons can show how light, framing, and geometric detail give each chamber a distinct presence while maintaining a shared visual language.

references.heading: Related work — Hollow Knight
references.copy: [Hollow Knight](https://www.hollowknight.com/) explores an ancient, forgotten kingdom through atmospheric environments and encounters with its inhabitants. It offers a relevant comparison for Raven's portrayal of a civilisation after its fall. The reference here concerns the traces of former grandeur and gradual discovery of a world's past, with Raven expressing these ideas through conversations and picture puzzles.
